subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or keep default steering boundary-based?
rationale: The choice affects shared agent runtime semantics, Codex app-server contracts, channel-visible behavior, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported behavior and use narrower fixes only to ensure messages reach existing model-boundary steering.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof and channel/runtime compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the protected replacement attempt and shared active-run steering history that most directly overlaps the product choice.
